evidence.title: Renters get some good news
evidence.excerpt: Minister for Regional Development Fiona Nash said the Australian Government was investing $7.25 million towards the project to provide Norlane with high quality, accessible social infrastructure.
evidence.contextNote: The passage names Norlane and the Australian Government; the extraction represents the place's residents as the Norlane community actor. It reports an investment, not a measured community outcome.

evidence.title: Derelict school's rebirth
evidence.excerpt: Baptcare has bought the former Norlane Primary School site on Robin Ave and this week won $7.25 million in Commonwealth support.

evidence.title: Boosting the war on drugs [Geelong Edition]
evidence.excerpt: TWO Geelong drug and alcohol treatment programs have received almost $100,000 each in Federal Government funding. The Bridgelink Program, which provides intensive case management to homeless women experiencing drug and alcohol-related issues, will receive $99,830.

evidence.title: Boosting the war on drugs [Geelong Edition]
evidence.excerpt: TWO Geelong drug and alcohol treatment programs have received almost $100,000 each in Federal Government funding. The Eunike Program, which provides a supported accommodation program for women seeking to maintain a substance-free lifestyle, will receive $99,830.

evidence.title: The Gordon key in turning work future [Geelong Edition]
evidence.excerpt: In 2014, The Gordon worked with Alcoa workers to plan for their future career pathways.

evidence.title: The Gordon key in turning work future [Geelong Edition]
evidence.excerpt: With the shift to a more knowledge-based economy for Geelong, the longstanding partnership between The Gordon and Deakin University is critical to providing our community with the higher level skills required for the jobs of the future.

evidence.title: Workers making transition to future
evidence.excerpt: The Ford Transition Project, backed by Auto Skills Australia, $5 million Federal Government funding and support from Gordon TAFE has involved case managing more than 300 workers, aiming to help many recognise their skills for future employment and find additional skills where necessary.
evidence.contextNote: The report describes the Ford Transition Project and Gordon TAFE support. Its case-management figure refers to the project as a whole, not an outcome attributed to The Gordon alone.

evidence.title: Tech school architects chosen
evidence.excerpt: The Geelong Tech School will be operated by The Gordon Institute.

evidence.title: Healthy future ahead [Geelong Edition]
evidence.excerpt: The WDC -- set up as part of the Victorian Government's $11 million Skilling the Bay initiative -- assists retrenched workers and their families with advice, information and counselling on careers, retraining and job opportunities.
evidence.contextNote: The passage refers to 'WDC'; the stored actor name expands this as Geelong Workforce Development Centre and maps it to The Gordon. The excerpt does not itself establish that institutional equivalence.

stories.title: The network behind food support
stories.description: A foundation, a fundraising campaign and food-relief organisations appear together in reporting about support for Geelong people. Cafes and a bakery widen this picture of local participation.
stories.takeaway: Food support brings charities, local businesses and relief organisations into a shared local effort.

stories.title: Education, government and workers
stories.description: The Gordon connects government, another education institution and groups of workers in reporting about skills and career transitions. Context adds the Geelong Tech School and a worker-transition project.
stories.takeaway: Education institutions connect public investment with people preparing for changing work.

steps.title: An education–government connection
steps.text: A May 2015 passage describes government working with The Gordon on apprenticeship programs for train and tram engineers.

steps.title: Institutions meet worker groups
steps.text: The reporting describes a longstanding Gordon–Deakin partnership and career advice for retrenched workers through the Workforce Development Centre, mapped to The Gordon in this network.

steps.title: Career pathways in a changing economy
steps.text: The Gordon worked with Alcoa workers to plan future career pathways. The surrounding context also connects it with the Geelong Tech School and the Ford Transition Project.

stories.title: Partnerships around GROW
stories.description: Follow a small selection around GROW, Give Where You Live and G21. The reporting describes a joint initiative across organisational boundaries.
stories.takeaway: Local organisations, public institutions and business commitments come together around a shared jobs initiative.

steps.title: A joint initiative
steps.text: An August 2015 excerpt describes GROW as a joint initiative of Give Where You Live and G21. Read the words behind their connection.

steps.title: The program in the network
steps.text: GROW appears as a distinct actor alongside its partners. The records describe a partnership and a funding pledge around a shared jobs initiative.

steps.title: A wider circle of participation
steps.text: A 2016 report describes a council-funded employment project with GROW and neighbourhood centres. The wider context also records compact signatories committing to invest in local businesses and people.

stories.title: National support, local places
stories.description: Reporting about a Norlane redevelopment links Australian Government support, Baptcare and the Norlane community. Nearby selected ties show other federal commitments to local support programs.
stories.takeaway: National institutions become part of a local network through specific commitments to organisations and places.

steps.title: A national commitment to a local site
steps.text: A May 2015 report says Baptcare bought the former Norlane Primary School site and won $7.25 million in Commonwealth support. The Australian Government and Baptcare occupy different scope bands.

steps.title: The community named in the report
steps.text: An April 2016 report describes Australian Government investment in accessible social infrastructure for Norlane. The extraction represents Norlane residents with the Norlane community node.

steps.title: Local organisations and community places
steps.text: The same 2016 report identifies Baptcare and the Australian Government as funders of the planned project. Separate commitments to Bridgelink and Eunike widen the picture of national support for local services.

stories.title: Helping people after the flood
stories.description: Reports after Geelong's 27 January 2016 flood describe crews working together, residents seeking assistance and practical support for people facing immediate needs.
stories.takeaway: Cooperation becomes tangible in rescue requests, clean-up work and help with the costs of recovery.

steps.title: Crews work together
steps.text: On 29 January, the reporting describes eight council crews helping the SES divert traffic and clear debris from council roads.

steps.title: Residents seek help
steps.text: A 30 January report records more than 350 requests for SES assistance in the Geelong area and 15 rescue calls during the wild weather and flash floods. The source's Geelong residents are mapped to the community node.

steps.title: Practical help with recovery
steps.text: A 4 February report says residents would not pay tip fees under an assistance program. Its selected context also records state grants for immediate needs such as food, water and shelter.
